messages:
maria: Heads-up — customer X onboarded BYOK yesterday and hit us with a late ask: they need all HSM wrap/unwrap events forwarded to their SIEM via syslog and want operator RBAC tightened so only 2 named people can perform rewraps. Thinking through compliance impact (SOC2 + ISO) and runtime feasibility. Any constraints?

jonathan: For syslog, we currently export key lifecycle events to our central ELK. We can add a syslog forwarder but need to confirm PII/filtering and throughput — their SIEM expects TLS over 6514 and a specific JSON schema.

samir: RBAC-wise, our BYOK flow already separates 'import' vs 'wrap' abilities, but operator role surface is large. We can add a scoped role like `byok_rewrap_operator` tied to vault KMS ops. Question: do they want cross-account to actually receive logs with key IDs? That may leak tenant mapping.

maria: They asked for key provenance (key id + operation + operator-id + timestamp). Legal said that's ok if we pseudonymize tenant ids. Also they insist on HSM firmware hash in logs for attestation.

jonathan: small nit: their SIEM wants a field named `hsm_firmware` and `wrap_session_id`. We'll need to map internal fields. Ops-bot, any rate limits to syslog forward?

ops-bot: Syslog forwarder currently caps at 500 events/sec per node. Alerts at 450/sec.

luis: If we pseudonymize tenant -> we should keep a mapping in a sealed audit store (for legal) but not send it to the customer. That satisfies the audit trail without exposing other tenants. Also we should consider encrypting syslog stream with their public cert; storing TLS certs for customers is supported.

samir: For RBAC, two practical changes: 1) add a scoped role with MFA + time-bound JIT granting, 2) require dual-operator approval for rewraps in production. Both are doable but need UI/ops hooks. Dual-approval is extra latency during incidents.

maria: Compliance ask: need retention 7 years for these logs for this customer (their regulator). Our retention policy default is 1 year. Can we carve out a customer-specific retention?

jonathan: We can set per-tenant index lifecycle policy, yes, but storage cost will increase. Need finance sign-off. Also confirm whether we store the full KV-cache traces — regulator only asked for wrap events, not request payloads.

samir: Vulnerability triage: if we add a syslog forwarder, ensure it runs in an isolated subnet with egress-only to their SIEM. Also bump audit logging level to include firmware hash collection — that may require HSM vendor patch (we'll open ticket).

maria: Action items summary: 1) samir to draft RBAC changes (scoped role + dual approval + JIT flow) 2) jonathan to prototype syslog forwarder mapping to their JSON schema and TLS cert ingestion 3) luis to propose pseudonymization + sealed mapping design 4) ops-bot to monitor forwarder perf and set alarms.

jonathan: Quick prototype config snippet for mapping (will iterate):
```
syslog_forwarder:
  destination: "tls://siem.customerx.example:6514"
  mapping:
    key_id: event.key_id
    operator: event.operator_id
    firmware: event.hsm_firmware_hash
    session: event.session_id
```

luis: FYI I'll loop in finance/legal for retention and PII concerns.

maria: @samir please estimate effort for RBAC + dual-approval and put a short PRD in #eng-security by EOD tomorrow. :eyes:

samir: Will do. One more technical note: for dual-approval we can leverage existing runbook service but need audit-proof evidence of both approvals. I'll include cryptographic attestation in the PRD.

maria: thanks — last thing: if vendor HSM firmware can't expose hash, we may need hardware attestation workaround (signed manifest). Include fallback in the PRD.

ops-bot: Created incident ticket INC-2024-447 for vendor HSM firmware request.
